column6: What is the difference between concentration and mindfulness?
The point that includes versus the point that excludes.|Ajahn Sumedho

I feel like the point you're making about an exclusive versus an inclusive unification or one-pointedness is in line with the way I've been practicing Zazen. ... [Mindfulness and concentration both feel like they have the quality of open awareness that is inclusive. ... Is concentration a more developed kind of mindfulness?
If you live long enough and you start to have Alzheimer's or dementia, if you're well-practiced throughout your whole life, you'll still be grounded in something, right?
Despite having dementia, Venerable Mahāghosānanda attends a meeting of Buddhist leaders at Spirit Rock Meditation Center. Abhayagiri monks look after him and delight in his presence.
When Ajahn Chah was sick, his cognitive functions deteriorated, but his citta was unwavering.
You don't have to worry about Ajahn Chah. His mind is bright and pure.|Ajahn Poot
The mind is another sense base. It's not who you are.

How do you deal with the fear of renunciation and sacrifice that you do on the path of practice? Giving things up that are familiar and comfortable, or even that you know are uncomfortable, but there's still that dukkha around it. Or after you've given up, the mind can proliferate on these subjects a lot. What has your experience been like?
Everything I've ever let go of has claw marks on it.|David Foster Wallace
Just sweep the leaves in front of your broom.
